source.phase_assignment: official_draw_context_supplied_by_parent; slate/boundary not revalidated in this outlet-focused review

rules: All point event timestamps remain NA. Brackets are sampled visibility candidates pending parent refinement, not claims of exact physical event time.
A before sample means the positive visible state is not established, sometimes because blur or a changing component obstructs it; it is not proof the physical state was absent.
Native frame timing is retained but images reviewed are quarter-resolution previews; do not claim native-pixel precision or one-frame event localization.
No permanent isolation, electrical control onset, complete gate state, physical paddle angle or RPM is inferred.
Overlay first readable and overlay slot filled are distinct graphics definitions. Neither is a capture clock.
No reviewer discrepancy distribution or human calibration is available. Same-model review does not provide independent experimental replication.

events.note: Finger is already in contact with the control in close-up samples1113.412300–1114.012900; preceding wide shot does not resolve contact onset. No onset timestamp assigned.
The initial control close-up cuts to an outlet-only shot; the globe/outlet input boundary and the preceding mechanism state are not continuously visible.

First clear yellow ball visibility in the collector/outlet housing. A moving component can conceal earlier occupancy, so this bounds the visible-state transition and is not certified physical entry time.
A ball is visibly held below the mixing chamber in the lower collector compartment. This is an observed separated-position proxy, not proof of permanent isolation or a known one-way gate plane.
Internal gate topology, one-way plane and irreversibility are not established. A visibly separate ball is insufficient to certify permanent isolation.

A ball transitions from the outlet housing toward the inclined result channel. Preview blur/overlay and the camera cut require a deliberately conservative candidate bracket; parent must refine consecutive native frames. Same outlet/result view remains visible.
First clearly readable new broadcast number in reviewed samples, including moving graphic before its final slot when readable. This is a television graphics event only, not physical selection.
First reviewed sample with the new broadcast number fully placed in its result slot; recorded separately from first appearance.
No audio listening or ASR timing was used by this reviewer.
